content.title: A Dua Filled with Tawakkul Can Turn the Impossible into the Possible!
content.subtitle: The tears of a devoted lover on the dusty desert road and a moving tale of divine aid
content.body:
Looking at the Jeddah–Jazan highway on a scorching afternoon, it felt as though the desert was breathing fire. On that blazing Ramadan day, I accompanied my sponsor to distribute Zakat in an impoverished coastal village. In that shimmering heat, a lone silhouette emerged in the distance—an elderly man in his seventies walking with frail steps yet unwavering conviction. His clothes were covered in dust, and his lips were parched with thirst. Yet, upon his face rested an ethereal serenity that belongs only to a true lover of the Divine.

The Resolute Journey of a Destitute Lover

We stopped the car, approached him, and greeted him with Salam. Instantly, an unwearied smile graced his lips. When asked about his identity, he shared that he had traveled all the way from war-torn Yemen. Where was he headed? Without hesitation, he replied—to the Holy House of Allah, for Umrah. Why choose this perilous valley over legal routes? The old man answered simply, "Son, I lacked the two thousand Riyals for the security deposit. My entire wealth was merely two hundred Riyals. One hundred went for fare, and the last hundred rests in my pocket. So, I am crossing the rest of the journey on foot." He had been walking through this desert for six consecutive days. Remarkably, amidst this intense heat and exhausting journey, he was fasting!

Open Highways by Divine Decree

Stunned, we asked, "How did you pass through so many checkpoints? Did no one stop you?" The old man swore, "By the Great Lord, besides Whom there is no deity! I walked right past every checkpoint, yet no one stopped me." He added, "A while ago, a patrol took me to the police station. But when I said my sole purpose was visiting the House of Allah, they set me free." Hearing this sent chills through our spines; indeed, when the heart harbors pure love for the Baytullah, no earthly border can hold a soul back.

Divine Aid Soaked in Tears

Moved by his firm faith, my sponsor’s eyes welled with tears. He handed two Zakat envelopes to the elder. The old man thanked us humbly, unaware of what lay inside. When we said, "Father, please open the envelopes and secure the money," he opened them to find ten thousand Riyals and froze. Overwhelmed by shock and emotion, he collapsed onto the car seat. Tears poured down his cheeks like rain as he whispered, "Is all this truly for me? Such a vast sum, all mine?" After reviving him with water, he wept aloud, "In Yemen, I have a small house with land that I waqf for Allah. With my children, I built a mosque there. The structure is complete, but the flooring and finishing remain. I was constantly worried about where the funds would come from. Today, Allah bestowed it through you."

Provisions Like Birds and Boundless Tawakkul

Witnessing this, we could no longer hold back our tears. The words of the Prophet ﷺ came alive—whoever makes the Hereafter their goal, Allah grants richness in their heart and the world rushes to their feet. Deeply moved, the sponsor pressed two more envelopes into his hands. Clutching twenty thousand Riyals to his chest, the elderly pilgrim stood weeping, "Today, Allah delivered my provision just like a bird!" Truly, as the hadith proclaims: if you relied upon Allah with true reliance, He would provide for you just as He provides for birds—leaving empty-bellied at dawn and returning full at dusk. That miraculous desert noon bore witness: for the servant who surrenders all to the Lord, even burning sands turn into a bed of divine mercy.

Note: This incident occurred with an expatriate brother living in Saudi Arabia, collected from the Facebook wall of Dr. Abdur Rahman.
